title: Preface
summary: An FBI/Justice Department document dated December 1, 1966, forwarded by J. Edgar Hoover to Marvin Watson, Special Assistant to the President, enclosing a memorandum summarizing FBI files on the reaction of Soviet and Communist Party officials to President Kennedy's assassination. Subjects include Lee Harvey Oswald's Russian period, defection, suicide attempt, proposed 1963 Russia trip, and Mexico trip; the Warren Commission; Yuri Nosenko; Pravda and Izvestia; Progressive Labor; and FBI ultraright conspiracy theories and coup claims. Marked Top Secret and withheld.

title: REACTION ‘OF SOVIET -AND COMMUNIST PARTY OFPICIALS TO THE ASSASSINATION OF PRESIDENT JOHN F. KENNEDY
summary: A declassified TOP SECRET report says a reliable source in Russia, on December 4, 1963, relayed that Soviet officials and Communist Party leaders reacted to President Kennedy's assassination with shock, and church bells tolled in his memory. Officials believed a planned 'ultraright' U.S. conspiracy aimed at a coup, halting Soviet negotiations and attacking Cuba. The USSR went on national alert, fearing an irresponsible U.S. general might launch missiles. They judged the Communist Party USA an unlikely culprit.

title: REACTION OF SOVIET AND COMMUNIST PARTY OFFICIALS TO THE ASSASSINATION OF PRESIDENT JOHN F, KENNEDY
summary: Declassified FBI-style report on Soviet and Communist Party reactions to President Kennedy's assassination. Soviet officials called Lee Harvey Oswald a neurotic, disloyal man with no Soviet ties. Ambassador-level staff (Fedorenko) regretted Kennedy's death and expressed uncertainty about Lyndon Johnson. KGB New York chief Ivanov called for urgent investigation of possible organized plotting and ordered intelligence gathering on Johnson, including a 1965 instruction to probe claims Johnson was responsible for the assassination. Defector Yuri Nosenko described Oswald's KGB history: a 1959 defection attempt, a suicide attempt, a rejected 1963 re-entry request, and Soviet handling of the consular file. Gus Hall of the US Communist Party blamed the 'ultraright' and suggested Oswald may have worked for the FBI. The Worker criticized the Warren Report's treatment of right-wing conspiracy, and minor splinter groups were not found to oppose the Commission.

title: REACTION OF SOVIET AND COMMUNIST PARTY OFFICIALS .TO THE ASSASSINATION OF PRESIDENT JOUN F, KENNEDY
summary: Summarizes Soviet and Communist reactions to President Kennedy's assassination. Progressive Labor Party's 1963 publication questioned whether Oswald was the sole killer and suggested he was framed, faulting the Warren Commission's thoroughness. Soviet press criticized the Warren Commission Report: Pravda (1964) said it left doubts; Izvestia (1965) by V. Zorin called the case a riddle. New Times (1966) quoted Professor Richard Popkin's view that the assassination was a plot involving influential quarters.
